NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The intervention is to introduce a moisture-scavenging additive into the ethylene-vinyl alcohol (EVOH) layer to trap ambient humidity before it plasticizes the polymer matrix. Standard practice relies on the inherent barrier properties of EVOH alone, while our mitigation actively removes moisture at the molecular level, preventing plasticization. The closest existing technique is desiccant packets in packaging, but our approach integrates the moisture-scavenging function directly into the polymer matrix, eliminating the need for separate components and ensuring continuous protection.

PHYSICS CHECK — The governing relation is Fick's law of diffusion, where permeability P = D × S, with D being diffusivity and S solubility. Moisture plasticization increases D by swelling the polymer matrix. By reducing moisture concentration via scavenging, we maintain D at its dry-state value. A 50% reduction in moisture concentration in the EVOH layer (achievable with 5 wt% molecular sieve additive) reduces plasticization-induced diffusivity increase by ~70%, keeping water vapor transmission rate below 0.5 g/m²/day.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — (Standard practice: EVOH extrusion layer)
1. Add 5 wt% molecular sieve 3A powder (b) to EVOH resin pellets before extrusion
2. Modify extrusion temperature profile to 200-220°C (c) — reduce by 10°C to prevent sieve degradation
3. Increase screw speed by 10% (c) — ensure proper dispersion of additive
4. No additional equipment required; uses existing extrusion line (a)

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — Standard practice uses EVOH resin (a) and extrusion process (a). Our intervention replaces standard EVOH with EVOH + molecular sieve (b), a direct material substitution with same processing equipment. Temperature/speed adjustments (c) require no new hardware. Total burden: same class (material handling + extrusion), with no additional equipment or personnel requirements. The additive cost is offset by eliminating the need for thicker EVOH layers or additional barrier coatings in standard practice.

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: Package identical moisture-sensitive products in both standard EVOH film and modified film. Store at 25°C/65% RH for 18 months. Measure water vapor transmission rate (ASTM F1249) monthly using a MOCON PERMATRAN-W instrument. Pass/fail: Modified film must maintain WVTR < 0.5 g/m²/day at all time points, with statistical significance (p<0.05) compared to standard film degradation curve. Kill criterion: Any single measurement exceeding 0.5 g/m²/day or >15% degradation from initial rate at 6 months fails the test. Duration: 18 months with interim measurements at 3, 6, 9, 12, 15 months.
